qs.q: A patient presents with an anterior neck mass and is evaluated with thyroid function tests and fine needle aspiration cytology. Which of the following is a recognized cause of such a swelling?
qs.e: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is a common inflammatory cause of anterior neck swellings and goitre. The other options involve the kidney, ovary, or uterus respectively.

qs.q: What is the characteristic sequence of thyroid function tests (TFTs) in subacute (De Quervain's) thyroiditis?
qs.e: Subacute thyroiditis typically follows a triphasic course: an initial hyperthyroid phase (due to release of preformed thyroid hormone), followed by a hypothyroid phase (as thyroid hormone stores are depleted), and finally recovery to euthyroidism in most cases. It is often preceded by a viral upper respiratory infection and is associated with a markedly elevated ESR and very low radioactive iodine uptake.
